column1: # premise-meat: Organic is the floor; grass-fed, pasture seals show the animal lived outdoors.
# premise-eggs: Pick pasture-raised with a third-party seal over cage-free wording.
# premise-seafood: Wild with named species and origin first; shellfish live, scallops dry.

column4: AGA Grassfed seal; label reads 100% grass-fed and grass-finished
column5: AGA animals eat only grass and forage from weaning until harvest, on pasture, never given antibiotics.

column4: Whole cut in a sealed tray with AGA Grassfed seal and USDA Organic
column5: Organic rules require a feed ration of organic pasture and forage, so the organic seal covers what the animal ate.

column4: Ground beef pack naming grass-finished; ratio printed beside the AGA seal
column5: Antibiotic-treated animals cannot be sold as organic, so the seal covers that too.

column4: AGA seal on pack with a short ingredient list
column5: AGA animals are fed only grass and forage and never given added growth hormones.

column4: First ingredient beef; AGA or organic seal on the bag
column5: Weston A. Price advises meat snacks made from grass-fed and finished meat with simple ingredients, and warns many carry substantial added sugar.

column4: Marrow bones from the counter, tagged grass-finished or AGA
column5: AGA animals graze pasture without confinement.

column4: Liver or heart pack carrying an organic or AGA seal
column5: Weston A. Price says sourcing is key for organ meats and points to pasture-raised, 100% grass-fed animals.

column4: Lamb tray stamped AWA pasture; chops with pale pink fat
column5: AWA guarantees animals live outdoors on pasture or range for their entire lives.

column4: Pack lists bison only; AGA Grassfed mark beside the cut
column5: AGA requires a 100% grass diet from weaning until harvest.

column4: Tray names deer and shows an inspected and approved mark
column5: Weston A. Price notes deer forage on wild plants and are not raised in confinement.

column4: Only if label says pasture-raised with a humane seal
column5: Pasture-raised veal means calves raised on open pasture beside the mother, never in feedlots.

column4: Bone-in, skin-on breast with USDA Organic plus Certified Humane Pasture Raised
column5: Certified Humane pasture raised requires 108 square feet per bird outdoors, matching AWA.

column4: Whole bird with AWA seal; skin cream-yellow, no basting solution listed
column5: AWA guarantees outdoor pasture life for the whole animal.

column4: Wings with skin intact, pack states organic and pasture-raised
column5: Organic livestock eat feed grown under certified organic rules including pasture.

column4: Ingredients list only chicken and salt; organic seal on sticker
column5: Organic livestock eat a feed ration of organically produced agricultural products, including pasture and forage.

column4: Tag reads not basted; USDA Organic, Certified Humane Pasture Raised
column5: Organic turkeys are fed certified organic feed with pasture and forage.

column4: Pack states thigh and breast meat only, organic seal
column5: Antibiotic-treated birds cannot carry the organic label.

column4: Whole duck with skin on and AWA or organic seal
column5: AWA covers duck standards and requires pasture or range living.

column4: Chop pack without added solution; AWA or Certified Humane pasture seal
column5: AWA guarantees pigs live outdoors on pasture or range.

column4: Ingredients show pork, salt, celery powder only; pasture seal on pack
column5: The USDA rule lets 'Uncured' appear in the name only for products cured without synthetic nitrite.

column4: Whole-muscle ham whose name begins Uncured, ingredients listing salt and pork
column5: 'Uncured' must lead the product name under federal curing rules.

column4: Name reads Uncured turkey bacon; turkey listed first
column5: 9 CFR 317.17 requires the term Uncured before the product name on products cured without nitrite.

column4: Dry-cured wording on pack; ingredient list is pork and salt
column5: 'Uncured' wording is regulated product-name text for cured meats.

column4: Casing ingredients short; third-party welfare seal for outdoor access
column5: AWA guarantees pasture or range life for the whole animal.

column4: Uncured on the deli label; whole roast sliced fresh
column5: The word 'Uncured' must precede the product name on cured-style meats.

column4: Carton shows USDA Organic and Certified Humane Pasture Raised
column5: Pasture raised under Certified Humane means 108 square feet per hen versus 2 for free range.

column4: Cage-free only on carton, no outdoor access seal
column5: Certified Humane free range needs 2 square feet outdoors; cage-free carries no outdoor figure.

column4: Certified Humane or AWA Pasture Raised plus USDA Organic seal
column5: Certified Humane and AWA pasture-raised standards both specify 108 square feet per bird.

column4: Carton names duck and says pastured
column5: The Weston A. Price shopping guide lists pastured duck eggs among its best eggs.

column4: Carton lists egg whites only, with an organic seal
column5: No holistic source found for egg whites.

column4: Label says wild Alaskan; sockeye flesh deep red
column5: COOL law requires wild or farm-raised printed on fresh and frozen fish.

column4: Blue MSC fish checkmark with a chain-of-custody code
column5: The MSC mark is only for wild fish from certified fisheries.

column4: Tag spells wild or farm-raised plus country and catch method
column5: Fish sellers must label wild or farm-raised by federal rule.

column4: ASC logo on pack when fish is farmed
column5: ASC says seafood carrying its label on pack was farmed with care.

column4: Whole trout with bright eyes and shiny skin
column5: No holistic source found for fresh whole trout.

column4: Bag names Gulf or US wild shrimp, shell on, no additives
column5: Wild or farm-raised plus origin must appear on the label.

column4: Pacific cod fillet, grey-brown skin side, species named on tag
column5: Pacific cod are grayish-brown with a paler belly, helping check the species.

column4: Pack says wild pollock fillet, not formed from minced pieces
column5: Pollock is also made into surimi, so fillet wording matters.

column4: Label says pole-caught, troll-caught, FAD-free or school-caught
column5: Seafood Watch points to canned tuna with pole-caught, troll-caught, FAD-free, free school or school-caught on the label.

column4: Sardines labelled skin and bones, wild-caught, in olive oil
column5: Weston A. Price recommends sardines with skin and bones as high in vitamin D and a good source of calcium.

column4: Can names sardines
column5: A Weston A. Price article lists sardines among a short list of recommended fish for low mercury.

column4: Mackerel with vivid stripes still bright; sardines with shiny skin
column5: Mackerel colour fades quickly after death, so dull stripes signal age.

column4: Jar lists salmon roe and salt only
column5: Weston A. Price calls roe a rich source of vitamins A and D, very long-chain fatty acids, and zinc.

column4: Dry-packed scallops sitting without milky liquid in the tray
column5: Dry scallops have not been soaked in sodium tripolyphosphate.

column4: Live lobster moving its claws; frozen tails hard with no ice glaze
column5: American lobster is mainly sold live or frozen.

column4: Live crab showing leg movement
column5: Foodal advises choosing live crabs that are active and moving, and heavy in the hand.

column4: Shells close when tapped; harvest tag on the bag
column5: Pacific Coast Shellfish Growers say oysters should always be tightly closed and mussels should close when tapped.

column4: Label says wild or farm-raised, with origin; sold chilled
column5: Fish and shellfish must be labeled to indicate whether they are wild or farm-raised.

column4: Whole fish on ice with clear eyes and species sign
column5: Whole fish on ice should look bright-eyed with shiny skin, as the sardine guidance describes.
